The shot transitions to show a plane superimposed over the lights of the aurora borealis. The lights fade into a view of the horizon. This video segment provides a tour of an Antarctic Submillimeter Telescope and Remote Observatory, named ASTRO, which operated from 1995 to 2005. A woman narrator explains how sensitive instruments pick up signals, while the shot focuses on the telescope's silver, dish-shaped mirror and its components. Next, a wider shot shows three people on the roof of a white building with the telescope, waving their arms excitedly in celebration. A polar astronomer named Tony Stark is seen pointing to the main mirror of the telescope and explaining how light is focused and sent to a receiver room downstairs. He wears a black winter hat with fur around the hood, and a white glove. The video displays various other shots of telescope components, the receiver room filled with equipment, and the snowy landscape of the South Pole station. The camera pans to show the bright sun in the sky. The scene transitions to an animation of a pink and red galaxy. The video conveys the significance of ASTRO as a pioneer in millimeter and submillimeter wavelength radio telescopes.
